bottom_line: In older patients with systolic ischemic heart failure, rosuvastatin vs placebo did not reduce the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.83 to 1.02; P = 0.12).
implications: These data support that, in this population, rosuvastatin did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.02; P = 0.12) or death from any cause (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.86 to 1.05; P = 0.31), while the prespecified secondary analysis showed fewer total hospitalizations for cardiovascular causes (2193 vs 2564; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Randomized trial in older (≥60 years) patients with NYHA II–IV ischemic systolic heart failure comparing rosuvastatin 10 mg daily vs placebo.
major_points.quote: A total of 5011 patients at least 60 years of age with New York Heart Association class II, III, or IV ischemic, systolic heart failure were randomly assigned to receive 10 mg of rosuvastatin or placebo per day.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary composite outcome was death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.

major_points.text: Median follow-up was 32.8 months; primary outcome was not significantly different between groups.
major_points.quote: During a median follow-up of 32.8 months, the primary outcome occurred in 692 patients in the rosuvastatin group and 732 in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.83 to 1.02; P = 0.12)

major_points.text: Death from any cause was not significantly different between groups.
major_points.quote: and 728 patients and 759 patients, respectively, died (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.86 to 1.05; P = 0.31).

major_points.text: Prespecified secondary analysis found fewer cardiovascular hospitalizations in the rosuvastatin group (total hospitalizations).
major_points.quote: In a prespecified secondary analysis, there were fewer hospitalizations for cardiovascular causes in the rosuvastatin group (2193) than in the placebo group (2564) (P<0.001).

major_points.text: No excess muscle-related or other adverse events were reported with rosuvastatin.
major_points.quote: No excessive episodes of muscle-related or other adverse events occurred in the rosuvastatin group.

absolute_effects.text: Primary outcome event rate (per 100 patient-years) in each arm: placebo 12.3 vs rosuvastatin 11.4.
Death from any cause event rate (per 100 patient-years) in each arm: placebo 12.2 vs rosuvastatin 11.6.
Any coronary event event rate (per 100 patient-years) in each arm: placebo 10.0 vs rosuvastatin 9.3.

subgroups.quote: The effect of treat­ ment was consistent across all subgroups of pa­ tients with prespecified risks, with no indication of harm in any subgroup

analysis_methods.text: All data were analyzed in the intention-to-treat population defined as all patients who received a bottle of study drug.
analysis_methods.quote: All data were analyzed in the intention-to­ treat population, which was defined as all pa­ tients who received a bottle of a study drug.

analysis_methods.text: Main analyses used log-rank test and an unadjusted Cox proportional-hazards model to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals.
analysis_methods.quote: The main analyses were performed with the use of the log-rank test for the comparison of the study groups and an unadjusted Cox proportional-haz­ ards model to calculate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals

analysis_methods.text: Power was 90% to detect the prespecified reduction with two-sided alpha 0.05, requiring 1422 patients with the primary outcome.
analysis_methods.quote: To provide a statistical power of 90% to detect such a reduction in risk with a two-sided alpha of 0.05, 1422 patients with the primary outcome were needed.

analysis_methods.text: Estimated that 4950 patients would be needed based on recruitment and follow-up assumptions.
analysis_methods.quote: we estimated that 4950 patients would be needed on the basis of a recruitment period of 16 months and a fol­ low-up of 35 months.

analysis_methods.text: Three planned interim analyses were performed at 25%, 50%, and 75% of expected primary events and deaths with adjustment of overall significance level.
analysis_methods.quote: Three planned interim analyses were performed when 25%, 50%, and 75% of the total expected primary events and deaths had occurred, with appropriate adjustment of the overall significance level.

trial_conduct.quote: The trial was monitored by an independent data and safety monitoring board

trial_conduct.text: Serious adverse events were adjudicated by an independent committee to identify outcomes using prespecified definitions.
trial_conduct.quote: All serious adverse events were adjudicated by an independent committee to identify study outcomes according to prespeci­ fied definitions.

trial_conduct.text: Study was stopped as planned on the date that 1422 primary events were anticipated.
trial_conduct.quote: The study was stopped, as planned, on the date that 1422 primary events were antici­ pated (May 20, 2007).

criticisms.text: The trial studied older patients with moderate-to-severe heart failure, which the authors present as a limitation.
criticisms.quote: Our trial had some limitations. We studied older patients with moderate-to-severe heart fail­ ure

criticisms.text: Authors state they did not investigate patients with nonischemic heart failure or preserved ejection fraction.
criticisms.quote: We did not investigate two other important groups of patients with heart failure: those with nonischemic heart failure and those with a preserved ejection fraction.

criticisms.text: Authors note they may not have followed patients long enough to see a beneficial effect.
criticisms.quote: Another possibility is that we did not follow patients long enough to see a beneficial effect of treatment.
